findings.claim: Wave 1 PT-2 and decision 4: two Grok medium none probes at about $11-17 each, $22-34 in total [I], launched with an external watcher.
findings.problem: The credit ask is a point estimate with no hard bound. The harness says Grok has no spend cap, the default --timeout is 10800 s and --max-resumes is 20, so a watcher that never fires leaves a run uncapped for up to 3 h. The probes run 36-50 minutes, and LEARNINGS records that background tasks are killed at about 30 minutes. A kill splits the wide window being measured. The resume also replays work, and a killed session reports no cost, so the real spend cannot be reconstructed. The plan names no launch mode, no --timeout, no --max-resumes and no handling of the kill.
findings.evidence: test/shiploop_e2e/run.py parser: --max-budget-usd 'claude only; grok has no spend cap', --timeout default 10800, --max-resumes default 20. test/shiploop_e2e/LEARNINGS.md: 'killed at 1798 s by the 30-minute background-task limit', 'Launch long runs as background tasks ... never detach with nohup', 'a killed session reports no cost', per-stage minutes omit the kill-to-resume gap, and c1/c2 interrupt runs cost $25.85 against $8.60-11.20 uninterrupted because the killed session's work is replayed.
findings.fix: Put the bound in the ask. Name the --timeout and --max-resumes values for each probe, the launch mode (Desktop background task), and a worst-case dollar figure that includes one replayed resume. State that a killed Grok session's cost is unknown. Define the window from timeline or state stamps so a resume gap does not void the measurement. The owner approves the cap, not just the estimate.
